info.text:
US banks are sitting on $486 billion in paper (unrealized) losses on their investment securities.
That's up 48.8% from $326.7 billion in the prior quarter, the FDIC reported Nov 24, primarily because interest rates rose.
The losses equal 8.2% of what banks paid for those securities, and the FDIC says they remain well below their peak in Q3 2023 ($683.9 billion then).
Paper losses only become real if the securities are sold before they mature. Deposits are insured up to $250,000 per depositor, per insured bank, per ownership category.
Sources: FDIC Quarterly Banking Profile (Nov 24, 2026), Reuters.
News and education, not financial advice.
